maria: Heads-up — Halimeda reported a weird drop in numeric extraction after we merged their LoRA into `redwood/ember-7b` and ran an int4 quant pass.
ajay: drop as in accuracy or tokenization mismatch? any sample failures?
maria: accuracy on invoice amounts dropped ~12% absolute on our quickpack. Not tokenization mismatch exactly but truncation on number spans. Example in quickpack: expected "amount": "$1,234.56" -> model yields "amount": "$1,234" (missing cents).
eva: interesting. could be KV cache rounding from quantization or subtle weight collapse in LoRA heads. did you run the same merge at fp16 to compare?
maria: yes — fp16 merge is fine. The delta shows up only after int4 quant. I ran the quick eval pack on the merged adapter with quantized runtime (nvfuser int4 path).
maria: command I ran:
```
python tools/quick_eval.py \ 
  --model redwood/ember-7b+halimeda-lora \ 
  --quant int4 \ 
  --eval-pack evals/halimeda_smoke.json \ 
  --metric exact_amount_match --batch 16
```
benchbot: smoke run finished (2026-02-12 14:02 UTC). 200 examples. exact_amount_match: fp16=0.92, int4=0.80, int8=0.90. latency int4=32ms token, int8=45ms, fp16=120ms.
ajay: ok so int4 worse by 12 pts. int8 also slightly worse but less. can you paste a couple failing examples (input + both outputs)?
maria: pasted 3 failures below (input trimmed):
1) input: "Invoice total: $66.70" -> fp16: "$66.70", int4: "$66."
2) input: "Total due: USD 9,999.00" -> fp16: "9,999.00", int4: "9,999"
3) input: "Amount: 0.05 USD" -> fp16: "0.05", int4: "0.05" (this one ok)

maria: pattern looks like trailing decimals are being stripped for 2-digit cents, but 0.05 kept. maybe thresholding when formatting small fractional tokens.
eva: could be tokenizer merging cents into subtoken that gets dropped under int4 noise. try re-running with tokenizer debug (show token ids) and with `--preserve-decimals` postproc off/on.
ajay: also try running merge with different LoRA alpha scaling (we merged with alpha=32). maybe int4 interacts with high alpha.
maria: starting A/B runs now: (a) int4 w/alpha=32, (b) int4 w/alpha=8, (c) int8 w/alpha=32. will post results.

(40m later)
maria: results:
- int4 alpha=32: exact=0.80
- int4 alpha=8: exact=0.86
- int8 alpha=32: exact=0.90

maria: lowering alpha recovered 6 pts on int4. so interaction looks real.
eva: that suggests LoRA scaling amplifies small int4 quant noise. two short-term mitigations: reduce alpha for shipped adapter or pin model to int8 for Halimeda. long-term: add LoRA-aware quant calibration (per-adapter bias correction).
ajay: can we do a quick patch: publish two variants for customer — `halimeda-lora-int8` and `halimeda-lora-int4-lowalpha` and set routing policy to prefer int8 for invoice paths?
maria: yep. I created quick artifacts and updated eval pack with route tag. routing change is small – will push a canary tomorrow.
benchbot: artifact upload: halimeda-lora-int4-lowalpha (sha: a1b2c3), halimeda-lora-int8 (sha: d4e5f6). smoke evals triggered.

(15m)
benchbot: smoke evals done: int4-lowalpha exact=0.86, int8 exact=0.91. latency: int4-lowalpha=30ms, int8=46ms.
ajay: nice. can you add a short note in the onboarding doc: "Quantization interactions: LoRA alpha can amplify int4 noise causing numeric truncation; recommended defaults: alpha<=8 for int4, prefer int8 for numeric-sensitive workloads" — then tag customer success.
maria: done. docs PR -> https://git.redwood/halimeda-quant-guidance (draft)
eva: also file a small follow-up ticket for ops: add per-adapter quant calibration step to our optimize pipeline.
maria: filing now: RDW-ops-1129
ajay: thanks all. moving to canary tomorrow. :thumbsup!
